rationale: Experiment for the third investigation b2266ae85cad4e4db077a5615b2b892c-question-0. The harness follows the growth sequence the library documents, on a real single-voter cluster built by MakeCluster(1), and runs two cases in one execution: the named server is not running yet and is started only after the observation window, versus the same call with the named server running and wired first. The staged prefix uses only the library's own constructors (MakeCluster, NewInmemTransport, NewInmemStore, NewInmemSnapshotStore, NewRaft) and the public AddVoter API, so no production code is touched and no fault is injected. Native local feedback on this harness in a scratch copy inside draft showed the expected split between the cases, but the retained execution decides.

scope.description: Two subtests, absent_server and control_present_server. Each starts a one-voter cluster with MakeCluster(1), records the leader, its state, term, last index and the configuration, then calls the public AddVoter on the leader for a second server whose address comes from a fresh in-memory transport. In the absent case that transport is unwired and no raft runs on it; in the control the named server's raft is created and both transports are connected before the call. Each case then samples every 25 ms for 1500 ms: the original node's state, term, commit index and last index, whether the AddVoter future has completed and with what error, and whether the config entry index (recorded last index plus one) is committed. Afterwards a bounded client write is attempted, then the named server is started (in the absent case) and both cases record whether the configuration commits and a leader exists again within 4 s.
assumptions: Bootstrap a single voter and grow it with AddVoter is the sequence BootstrapCluster's documentation recommends, so the staged input follows the library's own guidance rather than an invented operator error.
The named server's identity and address are well formed (the ID is the address-derived ID of protocol version 3), and only its availability differs between the two cases.
In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss, so a refused RPC means the peer was not wired, not that a network fault intervened.
excluded: No production code is modified and no fault is injected.
No snapshot, restart or manual recovery path is exercised; the recovery observation only brings the named server up.

experiment.prefix: Each subtest prints CA_EVENT lines: growth_before (leader, state, term, commit and last index, configuration, named server identity and whether it is up, and the expected configuration entry index), growth_window (sampled state, term, commit and last index arrays, how many samples saw a Leader, whether the AddVoter future completed and its error, plus final values and whether the configuration entry committed), growth_write_attempt (the error of a bounded client write) and growth_recovery (whether the configuration committed and a leader exists after the named server is started, with the nodes' states and the elapsed time).
